Pharmacokinetics After intravenous injection of carbetocin, firm uterine contrac- tion occurs within 2 minutes and lasts for several hours. Carbe- tocin undergoes a biphasic elimination, with a terminal elimina- tion half-life of about 40 minutes. Less than 1% of a dose is excreted unchanged by the kidney. Carbetocin is distributed into breast milk. Uses and Administration Carbetocin is a synthetic analogue of oxytocin (p.2016) reported to have a longer duration of action. For the prevention of uterine atony and excessive bleeding after caesarean section under epi- dural or spinal anaesthesia, a single dose of 100 micrograms may be given by slow intravenous injection over 1 minute. Carbetocin must only be given after delivery of the infant, preferably before removal of the placenta. ◊ References. 1. Hunter DJS, et al.
